title: Room/reportAbuse on the provider's JMAP API (INVENTED): the client's AbuseReport relayed to the room's hub
description:
draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00 defines no way for a client to send a protocol-07 §5.9 AbuseReport; only the hub provider receives one and the client cannot reach a peer hub itself. INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC, until the draft has one (human bead filed with this one).

Chosen: Room/reportAbuse under urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:mimi, like Room/send. Arguments accountId, roomId (a Chat of the account has it, bound or not: a user removed from a room may still report what it received) and report, the unpadded base64url of a TLS-encoded AbuseReport the client assembled (the server sees no plaintext). The relay (follower/relay.rs, the provider's single identity point, decision mimid-1wgh.7.13) requires reportingUser to be the account's user, so mimid never sends an anonymous report; it routes to the room URI's authority (decision mimid-1wgh.7.5): this provider's hub in process with From this domain, or POST /reportAbuse/{roomId} through PeerClient (provider-authenticated as every peer request). Nothing is stored locally.

Answer: responseCode 'accepted' (the hub answered 200 or 201), 'notAllowed' (the hub refused by room policy: a mimid hub's 403 report-not-allowed, decision mimid-1wgh.56), 'unverifiedMessage' (a mimid hub's 422 unverified-abusive-message, decision mimid-1wgh.6.65), or 'refused' with status for any other 4xx from the hub; a 5xx or no answer is serverUnavailable and a malformed report invalidArguments (decision JM-6). The two named codes are read from the RFC 9457 problem type mimid's hub sends; another implementation's refusal is 'refused'.
notes: Mark 2026-11-18: always named; mimid never sends an anonymous report (kept as designed).
